process_area.title: Procurement Hedging, Forward Buying & Indexed-Pricing Strategy

fields.Participants: CFO, Treasury Manager, Procurement Director, Category Managers (links to VS-01), Risk (links to VS-21.2)
fields.Trigger: Annual program design (links to W3406); exposure review (W3404)

workflows.name: Commodity Mitigation Strategy Selection & Hedge Program Design

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Treasury/Procurement evaluate mitigation options per commodity" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-match of "matching the purchase plan" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document the hedge strategy and rationale for audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-548 (ensure controlled execution — Procurement Hedging, Forward Buying & Indexed-Pricing Strategy (PA-106.2).)
- operational: tenor matching and basis analysis; operational: hedge-ratio policy and board limit
Pain Points / Risks: - **Instrument-mismatch risk**: Hedging the wrong instrument/tenor leaves exposure or creates basis risk; mitigated by tenor matching and basis analysis
- **Over-hedge risk**: Hedging beyond physical exposure becomes speculation; mitigated by hedge-ratio policy and board limit
System Touchpoints: - Treasury/risk systems (links to VS-18/VS-21.2); merchandise plan (links to VS-101); policy repository (links to VS-186)

steps.activity: Treasury/Procurement evaluate mitigation options per commodity: financial hedge (futures/forwards/swaps), physical hedge / strategic inventory (W3410), indexed/floating contract (W3411), vendor pass-through clause (W3414), long-term supply agreement (W3415), or accept (self-insure); select based on exposure size (W3404), market liquidity, cost, accounting (W3413), and risk appetite (W3406)

Treasury design the hedge/mitigation program per selected commodity: hedge ratio (% of exposure covered), instrument, tenor matching the purchase plan (links to VS-101 W3284 receipts), trigger/threshold for activation, and the board authority limit (links to W3406); coordinate FX hedges (links to VS-18.3/W321) to avoid interaction gaps (W3408)

CFO/Board approve the mitigation program, authority matrix, and accounting designation (links to W3413); document the hedge strategy and rationale for audit (links to VS-21) and PFRS 9 hedge documentation (W3413)

fields.Participants: VP Merchandising, Buyers (links to VS-03.2), Supply Planning (links to VS-02.1), Treasury Manager, Finance (links to VS-101)
fields.Trigger: Market outlook (W3407) signaling price rise; supply-disruption risk (links to VS-69/VS-02.3)
fields.Volume: Top commodity-intensive A-items; ~5–15% incremental inventory in selected SKUs

workflows.name: Forward Buying, Strategic Inventory & Physical Hedge Execution

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-import of "identify forward-buy opportunities from the market outlook" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-file of "execute the forward buy via PO/blanket" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "track the forward-buy outcome vs market" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-548 (ensure controlled execution — Procurement Hedging, Forward Buying & Indexed-Pricing Strategy (PA-106.2).)
- operational: OTB control and carrying-cost analysis; operational: capacity check (links to VS-04) and 3PL option
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-stock risk**: Forward buy invalidated by demand drop ties up working capital (links to VS-105) and risks obsolescence; mitigated by OTB control and carrying-cost analysis
- **Storage-capacity risk**: Physical buy exceeds DC capacity; mitigated by capacity check (links to VS-04) and 3PL option
System Touchpoints: - PO/blanket (links to VS-03.2 W2C); DC/storage (links to VS-04); OTB (links to VS-101 W3283); cash (links to VS-18/VS-105)

steps.activity: Procurement/Merchandising identify forward-buy opportunities from the market outlook (W3407): commodities/SKUs with high price-rise probability, supply-allocation risk, or strategic importance; quantify the buy (volume, $, storage capacity links to VS-04, OTB impact links to VS-101 W3283) and the carrying-cost vs expected price-gain trade-off

Buyers/Merchandising execute the forward buy via PO/blanket (links to VS-03.2 W2C) or pre-buy agreement; coordinate storage at DC (links to VS-04) and financing/cash (links to VS-18/VS-105 WC impact); respect OTB and markdown-budget controls (links to VS-101 W3283/W3285) and inventory-turn guardrails (per profile §12.3)

Merchandising/Treasury track the forward-buy outcome vs market (W3403), realize the margin protection (W3417), manage aged strategic inventory (links to VS-05.3), and report physical-hedge performance to the review (W3416); clear residual stock via normal channels (links to VS-64/VS-05.3) if the thesis invalidates

fields.Participants: Procurement Director, Category Managers, Vendor (links to VS-03.3), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Finance
fields.Trigger: Strategic-vendor contract (links to VS-03.3); commodity exposure (W3401)

workflows.name: Indexed / Formula / Floating Vendor Contract Structuring

Automation Opportunity: - System continuous audit of "Category Managers/Procurement design the indexed/floating contract structure per vendor/commodity" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document the formula and index in the contract master" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "validate initial price, and set up the periodic re-price process" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-548 (ensure controlled execution — Procurement Hedging, Forward Buying & Indexed-Pricing Strategy (PA-106.2).)
- operational: simplicity and clear indices; operational: symmetric design and benchmarking (W3403)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Formula-complexity risk**: Over-complex formula is hard to administer/audit; mitigated by simplicity and clear indices
- **Asymmetric-clause risk**: Formula lets vendor raise but not lower price; mitigated by symmetric design and benchmarking (W3403)
System Touchpoints: - Vendor contract (links to VS-03.3/W230/W402); pricing master (links to W289); legal (links to VS-100.3); costing (links to VS-85)

steps.activity: Category Managers/Procurement design the indexed/floating contract structure per vendor/commodity: select the index (W3403), pricing formula (base + index multiplier), adjustment frequency (monthly/quarterly), cap/floor/collar, raw-material component weight (W3402), and notice/audit rights; benchmark to market practice (links to VS-03.3)

Procurement/Legal negotiate and execute the indexed contract clause (links to VS-100.3/W230), ensure it is enforceable, audit-able, and consistent with the exposure map (W3401) and pass-through strategy (W3414); document the formula and index in the contract master (links to W402)

Category Managers/Finance load the indexed formula into the price/cost master (links to W289 pricing master, W296 service/non-stock master), validate initial price, and set up the periodic re-price process (W3414); monitor formula integrity over the contract life

fields.Participants: Treasury Manager, CFO, Broker/Bank, Risk (links to VS-21.2), Finance (links to VS-17)

workflows.name: Financial Commodity Hedge Execution, Broker & Counterparty Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "counterparty, notional, strike/fix, maturity, premium" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document ISDA/master agreements" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Treasury roll/settle hedges at maturity, post cash collateral/margin as" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-548 (ensure controlled execution — Procurement Hedging, Forward Buying & Indexed-Pricing Strategy (PA-106.2).)
- operational: approved-list, limits, and diversification; operational: liquidity planning and authority limits
Pain Points / Risks: - **Counterparty-default risk**: Hedge counterparty fails; mitigated by approved-list, limits, and diversification
- **Margin-call/liquidity risk**: Margin/collateral calls strain cash (links to VS-18.1); mitigated by liquidity planning and authority limits
System Touchpoints: - Treasury dealing/risk systems (links to VS-18); bank/broker integration; GL (links to VS-17.1); hedge accounting (links to W3413)

steps.activity: Treasury execute the financial hedge (futures/forward/swap) per the program (W3409): select instrument/tenor matching the purchase plan (links to VS-101 W3284), obtain quotes from brokers/banks, transact within authority (links to W3406), and capture trade details (counterparty, notional, strike/fix, maturity, premium)

Treasury manage counterparty risk: select approved broker/bank counterparties, set exposure limits, monitor credit, and diversify; coordinate with FX hedge counterparties (links to VS-18.3/W317) to avoid concentration; document ISDA/master agreements (links to VS-100.3)

Treasury roll/settle hedges at maturity, post cash collateral/margin as required, reconcile settlements to GL (links to VS-17.1/W9A), and capture MTM for hedge accounting (W3413); feed hedge performance to the review (W3416)

fields.Participants: Finance Controller, Treasury Manager, External Audit (links to VS-21), CFO
fields.Trigger: Hedge execution (W3412); month-end close (links to VS-17.1/W9A)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "documentation at inception" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-classify of "reclassify to COGS/margin when the hedged purchase occurs, and document for audit" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-reconcile of "reconcile to physical purchase/price outcome" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-70 (ensure commodity exposure & hedge accounting accuracy.)
- operational: robust documentation and testing; operational: finance/audit review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hedge-accounting-disqualification risk**: Failed effectiveness test moves MTM to P&L and creates volatility; mitigated by robust documentation and testing
- **Disclosure-error risk**: Mis-stated hedge disclosure fails audit; mitigated by finance/audit review
System Touchpoints: - GL/hedge accounting (links to VS-17.1/W9A); treasury MTM (links to VS-18); FP&A (links to VS-17.4); audit (links to VS-21)

steps.activity: Finance/Treasury prepare PFRS 9 hedge documentation at inception: hedge relationship, risk-management objective, designated hedged item (purchase plan links to VS-101 W3284), hedge instrument (W3412), effectiveness test method, and accounting designation (cash-flow/fair-value hedge); obtain audit pre-clearance (links to VS-21)

Finance perform periodic (monthly) effectiveness testing and MTM: compute hedge effectiveness, post hedge MTM and effective/ineffective portions to GL (links to VS-17.1/W9A), reclassify to COGS/margin when the hedged purchase occurs, and document for audit; handle de-designation/discontinuance per PFRS 9

Finance/Treasury report hedge MTM, effectiveness, P&L impact, and OCI movement to FP&A (links to VS-17.4), executives (links to VS-33.2), and audit (links to VS-21); ensure disclosure consistency (links to VS-17) and reconcile to physical purchase/price outcome (W3416)

fields.Participants: Category Manager, Procurement, Vendor, Finance (links to VS-15/VS-85), Master Data (links to VS-29)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "validate against market benchmark and vendor submission" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document the change and audit trail" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor vendor compliance with the formula" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-548 (ensure controlled execution — Procurement Hedging, Forward Buying & Indexed-Pricing Strategy (PA-106.2).)
- operational: symmetric formula and benchmarking (W3403); operational: validation and audit trail
Pain Points / Risks: - **Surcharge-creep risk**: Vendors layer surcharges that never reverse; mitigated by symmetric formula and benchmarking (W3403)
- **Master-data-error risk**: Wrong cost/SRP update distorts margin (links to VS-101.3); mitigated by validation and audit trail
System Touchpoints: - Pricing master (links to W289); costing (links to VS-85); price management (links to VS-01.2); AP (links to VS-15.1)

steps.activity: Category Managers/Procurement compute the formula price/surcharge per indexed contract (W3411) using the latest index (W3403), contract formula, cap/floor, and raw-material weight; validate against market benchmark and vendor submission

Finance/Master Data update the item cost and SRP impact (links to W289 pricing master, VS-85 costing, VS-01.2 price management) in the ERP; AP picks up the new cost on subsequent invoices (links to VS-15.1); document the change and audit trail

Category Managers monitor vendor compliance with the formula (asymmetric pass-through, lagging reductions, surcharge creep), dispute deviations, and feed patterns to contract renewal (links to VS-03.3/W3415) and pass-through analytics (W3417)

fields.Participants: Procurement Director, Category Managers, VP Merchandising, Legal (links to VS-100.3), Finance, Vendor
fields.Trigger: Strategic-vendor relationship; commodity stabilization; capacity-security need

workflows.name: Long-Term Supply Agreement & Volume Commitment Negotiation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-post of "Category Managers/Procurement build the LTSA business case" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "Procurement/Finance administer the LTSA" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-548 (ensure controlled execution — Procurement Hedging, Forward Buying & Indexed-Pricing Strategy (PA-106.2).)
- operational: flexibility clauses and demand-planning accuracy (links to VS-02); operational: formula/floor design and periodic market-test
Pain Points / Risks: - **Volume-commitment risk**: Over-commitment ties BuildRight to unwanted volume; mitigated by flexibility clauses and demand-planning accuracy (links to VS-02.1)
- **Lock-in risk**: LTSA prevents benefiting from market drops; mitigated by formula/floor design and periodic market-test
System Touchpoints: - Vendor contract (links to VS-03.3/W402); legal (links to VS-100.3); vendor scorecard (links to VS-67); merchandise plan (links to VS-101)

steps.activity: Category Managers/Procurement build the LTSA business case: commodity stability, capacity/alloc security (esp. for steel/cement during construction booms or post-disaster links to VS-69), volume-commitment economics, price/formula terms (links to W3411), and duration; align to the merchandise plan (links to VS-101) and category strategy (links to VS-01)

Procurement/Legal negotiate and execute the LTSA: volume commitment/take-or-pay, price/formula (links to W3411), index/cap/floor, termination, force-majeure, quality/SLA, and exclusivity; ensure enforceability and risk allocation (links to VS-100.3/W230)

Procurement/Finance administer the LTSA: track volume vs commitment, compliance, pricing, renewal/cancellation, and performance (links to VS-67); report LTSA portfolio and risk to governance (W3406) and the category review (links to VS-01)

fields.Participants: CFO, Treasury Manager, Procurement Director, FP&A (links to VS-17.4), Risk (links to VS-21.2)

workflows.name: Hedge & Mitigation Performance Review and Strategy Adjustment

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Treasury/Procurement compile mitigation performance" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approve program updates" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-548 (ensure controlled execution — Procurement Hedging, Forward Buying & Indexed-Pricing Strategy (PA-106.2).)
- operational: objective benchmark and audit; operational: quarterly review and trigger-based adjustment
Pain Points / Risks: - **Counterfactual-bias risk**: Self-serving counterfactual overstates mitigation value; mitigated by objective benchmark and audit
- **Inertia risk**: Stale strategy fails to adapt to market change; mitigated by quarterly review and trigger-based adjustment
System Touchpoints: - Treasury/analytics (links to VS-18/VS-28.1); FP&A (links to VS-17.4); risk (links to VS-21.2); board reporting (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Treasury/Procurement compile mitigation performance: hedge MTM/settlement (W3412/W3413), forward-buy realized margin (W3410), indexed-contract price outcome vs market (W3411/W3414), LTSA performance (W3415), and the net margin-protection vs the no-mitigation counterfactual

CFO/Treasury evaluate strategy effectiveness vs objectives and risk appetite (W3406): hedge-ratio adequacy, basis risk, opportunity cost, and lessons; recommend strategy adjustments (ratio, instrument, vendor clause, LTSA)

CFO report mitigation performance and strategy to the executive committee (links to VS-33.2) and Audit Committee/Board (links to VS-36); ensure alignment with margin/EBITDA narrative (links to VS-101.3/VS-17.4) and approve program updates
